channel.title: Microsoft Foundry on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in Microsoft Foundry on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Developer CLI extension for Azure Document Intelligence and Content Understanding in Foundry Tools
item.description:
A public preview Azure Developer CLI extension adds azd ai cu commands for analyzing documents with Azure Document Intelligence and Content Understanding in Microsoft Foundry Tools. It can save analysis results as Markdown or JSON.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Cost controls for model and agent spending in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now supports cost controls for model and agent spending in public preview. Users can set spending or token budgets for a Foundry resource or project, with alerts sent via Azure Event Grid or new requests blocked when the threshold is reached.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: ai: What’s new in Microsoft Foundry | Ignite 2026
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry Ignite 2026 introduces updates across agents, developer tools, models, training, enterprise context, and governance. The post also emphasizes continuous improvement.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Updated Guardrails experience in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry Guardrails now exposes an updated experience in public preview for configuring agent runtime safety controls. It includes classifiers, deterministic rules, and LLM-based judges, and surfaces required controls when administrator policy enforces them.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Human annotation for agent evaluations in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Human annotation for agent evaluations is now in public preview in Microsoft Foundry. Reviewers can add ratings, tags, comments, and expected outputs to agent traces for evaluation workflows.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Agent insights in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now provides agent insights that analyze agent traces to identify recurring patterns and group related issues. Users can review an insight with its supporting traces, then use agent optimizer to test potential fixes.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Call model router without a deployment in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now supports calling the model router directly, without creating a deployment first. In supported regions, you can set the model to auto in Responses or Chat Completions requests to use Balanced routing by default.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Use the Messages API with model router in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Model router in Microsoft Foundry now supports the Messages API in public preview. This lets messages-based apps and coding tools use automatic model selection while preserving the Anthropic request and response format.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Use your model deployments with model router in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Model router in Microsoft Foundry now supports using your existing model deployments for routed requests in public preview. This lets you reuse existing capacity while the router chooses a model per request.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Model router now supports the Responses API protocol in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry’s model router now supports the Responses API protocol in general availability on both resource and project endpoints. Applications using Responses can point to the model router deployment name to enable automatic model selection.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Use model router with AI Gateway
item.description:
Azure AI Gateway now supports a model router in public preview for automatic model selection. For each request, it ranks models behind an alias using Microsoft Foundry, then combines that ranking with alias priorities and weights to choose a backend.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Governance policy guidance in Foundry Canvas and VS Code
item.description:
Governance policy guidance is now generally available in Foundry Canvas and the Foundry Toolkit for Visual Studio Code. As agents are built, both surfaces show relevant policies for agent types, models, toolboxes, and guardrails, including warnings.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Programmed Training in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Programmed Training is now in public preview in Microsoft Foundry. It provides an API for building custom post-training loops over open-weight models, with access available by request through a preview sign-up form.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Multi-turn evaluation in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now offers multi-turn evaluation in public preview. It lets you assess full agent conversations against quality standards instead of evaluating only individual responses.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: ai: Serve open models in production with Foundry Managed Compute
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry Managed Compute is now generally available for serving open models in production on dedicated GPUs. It supports Global and US or EU Data Zone deployments.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Build trusted autonomous agents for your team with Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry announces guidance for building trusted autonomous agents for teams, framing the problem as trust and governance rather than raw agent capability.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service at Ignite 2026: from pilot to production inside your enterprise boundaries
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry Agent Service added enterprise-focused hosted agent capabilities at Ignite 2026, including shared subnet IPs, private CA trust, network egress controls, deployment to customer-managed AKS clusters, resilient execution, and memory snapshots.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Browser Automation Tool in Microsoft Foundry : Ignite’26 Announcements
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry announced a browser automation tool for agents with enterprise-focused controls and browser session features. The update adds MCP action batching, Live View with Take control, session recording, VNet injection, browser proxy, profile reuse, secret management, and CAPTCHA handling.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: The Foundry Dev Pack is here: build Foundry agents your way
item.description:
Microsoft has made the Foundry Dev Pack generally available. It installs Microsoft Foundry developer tools locally in one package so you can build agents from an editor, terminal, or coding agent.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: What’s new in Foundry Agent Service at Ignite 2026
item.description:
Microsoft announces Ignite 2026 updates for Foundry Agent Service, focused on making agents more reliable in production by improving context handling, tool use, runtime resilience, and iterative improvement.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Build once, reuse across your agent fleet: Tools and Toolboxes in Foundry
item.description:
The post introduces Tools and Toolboxes in Foundry as a way to share agent capabilities across multiple production agents instead of wiring the same integrations separately for each one. It focuses on reducing duplicated instructions, dependencies, and setup work when scaling agent fleets.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Microsoft Foundry Support for Business Applications in Work IQ
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now generally available for Business Applications in Work IQ, helping developers build business-connected agents with less custom integration work. It is intended to turn enterprise data into actionable workflows.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: commandline: From custom infrastructure to hosted agents
item.description:
Novo rebuilt its clinical trials data agent on Microsoft Foundry, moving from custom infrastructure to hosted agents. The reported benefits are a simpler operating model, stronger session isolation, and a clearer path from tracing to evaluation and optimization.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: ai: When one pass isn’t enough: agentic mode in Azure Content Understanding
item.description:
The post introduces agentic mode in Azure Content Understanding for harder document-analysis tasks that need more than a single pass. It also explains when to use agentic mode instead of standard mode.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Microsoft Foundry extension for Azure Developer CLI is generally available
item.description:
The Microsoft Foundry extension for Azure Developer CLI is now generally available. It lets you set up, test, evaluate, and deploy hosted agents while keeping agent and deployment configuration with your code.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Bring Agentic Coding On-Device with Foundry Local
item.description:
Microsoft says Foundry Local now supports agentic coding directly on developer hardware. The post announces local on-device use of the Qwen3-8-27B model for this workflow.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: What’s new in Microsoft Foundry | October 2026
item.description:
October 2026 Microsoft Foundry updates include a Copilot harness preview, general availability for browser automation and hosted-agent resilience, a Decisions API, and SDK updates with chapter-linked Handoff demos. The post also points readers to Microsoft Ignite viewing on November 17-20.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness in Foundry Agent Service
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry is introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness in Foundry Agent Service as part of a shared execution foundation for agent experiences. It is meant to combine context, tools, execution environment, controls, and an agent loop, while preserving customer choice in supported options.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Cost management and tagging for Claude models in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now includes Claude model charges in Azure Cost Management with the rest of Foundry spend, and this is generally available. Previously, Claude charges were shown under SaaS instead of the Foundry resource used for deployment.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: ai: Announcing Azure AI Speech LLM 09-2026: Broader locale support
item.description:
Azure AI Speech LLM 09-2026 adds broader locale support and claims improvements in multilingual quality and latency. The post positions the update as an expansion of supported language/locale coverage.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: dotnet: Bring Your Own Model to the GitHub Copilot SDK with C#
item.description:
The GitHub Copilot SDK now supports BYOK, allowing apps to keep the agent runtime while routing model requests to a user-managed Microsoft Foundry or Azure OpenAI deployment. The post provides the full C# setup for this configuration.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: ai: Browser automation tool in Microsoft Foundry is now GA
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry’s browser automation tool is now generally available. It adds managed browsers, native toolbox integration, Live View, and human-in-the-loop control for automating tasks on public and private websites.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: What’s new in Microsoft Foundry | September 2026
item.description:
The September 2026 Microsoft Foundry post highlights updates across models, Routines, Tool Search, Model Router, and Insights. It presents these changes through a two-agent workflow that turns public releases into a Foundry developer changelog.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Azure Document Intelligence and Azure Content Understanding: a practical guide
item.description:
The post compares Azure Document Intelligence and Azure Content Understanding, focusing on extraction architecture, workload fit, layout capabilities, deployment options, and how to evaluate which service to use. It is a practical guidance piece rather than a feature announcement.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Why content extraction still matters in the GenAI era
item.description:
The post argues that as AI models improve, reliable content extraction becomes more important for trustworthy downstream use. It also contrasts Azure Content Understanding and Azure Document Intelligence, and previews what is next.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Control where your hosted agent connects with network egress in Foundry Agent Service
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry Agent Service now supports outbound network egress controls for hosted agents. You can define and attach an outbound policy, then monitor allowed and denied calls in Audit or Enforced mode.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: From Chatbots to Automated Agents: Routines in Microsoft Foundry Are Now Generally Available
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry’s Routines feature is now generally available, adding event-driven and scheduled automation so agents can monitor work, react to business events, and continue tasks over time instead of only responding in chat.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Enable and disable controls for Microsoft Foundry agents in Agent 365
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry agents can now be enabled or disabled from the Agent 365 governance surface in Microsoft Admin Center, and the feature is generally available. Administrators can control whether a Foundry agent is available for use across the tenant.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Network egress controls for hosted agents in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry public preview now supports network egress controls for hosted agents. Customers can define ordered outbound rules by destination host, including wildcard FQDNs like *.contoso.com, with allow or deny actions.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Publishing Microsoft Foundry agents to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams
item.description:
Publishing Microsoft Foundry agents to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams is now generally available. This gives Foundry developers a native path to make agents operational in the Microsoft 365 surfaces where users work.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: ai: Introducing Foundry Dev Pack: One Command to Start Building
item.description:
Microsoft announced Foundry Dev Pack, an all-in-one installer that prepares a machine for Microsoft Foundry development. It installs the tools needed for use in the terminal, VS Code, and coding agents.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: What’s new in Microsoft Foundry: July and August 2026
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry’s July and August 2026 update adds stable Hosted Agent and Toolbox SDK paths, Claude tools support on Azure-hosted deployments, and Model Router updates. It also notes local inference improvements and SDK migration items to review before upgrading.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog
